open: In the name of Allah. Assalamu alaikum, my dears. Come closer, tonight’s story is very beautiful.
s1a: Noah… Ilyas… do you remember? I told you about a baby who was in a little chest floating on a big river. Who would put a baby in a river?
s1b: Yes, who would do that? That’s dangerous!
s1c: Get warm and cosy, and you’ll find out. Tonight I’ll tell you about the Prophet Musa, peace be upon him. His name is mentioned in the Quran more than the name of any other prophet.
s2a: Do you remember the Prophet Yaqub? He had a second name: Israel, and that is why his descendants are called the Children of Israel. Many of them lived in Egypt, which was ruled by an unjust king: Pharaoh, “oppressing a sector among them, slaughtering their newborn sons”. And at that time, a mother from the Children of Israel had a child: Musa.
s2b: “And We inspired to the mother of Musa, ‘Suckle him; but when you fear for him, cast him into the river and do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and will make him one of the messengers.’” And for the chest: “Cast him into the chest.”
s2c: And where did the chest go?
s2d: Right to Pharaoh’s palace! Pharaoh’s wife saw the child and said: “He will be a comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he may benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son.”
s2e: “And We had prevented from him all wet nurses.” Then his sister, who had followed the chest in secret, came and said: “Shall I direct you to a household that will be responsible for him for you?” “So We restored him to his mother that she might be content and not grieve and that she would know that the promise of Allah is true.”
s2f: Wow! Allah brought him back to his mother!
s3a: Musa grew up in the palace. When he became a man, one day he had to leave Egypt, and he set out toward Madyan.
s3b: There, at a well, he saw two women waiting with their sheep until the shepherds had finished. “So he watered their flocks for them; then he went back to the shade and said, ‘My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You would send down to me, in need.’”
s3c: And did Allah send him something good?
s3d: And what good! The father of the two women invited Musa, and he married him to one of his two daughters, on the condition that Musa work for him eight or ten years.
s4a: And on the way back, “he perceived from the direction of the mount a fire. He said to his family, ‘Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I will bring you from there some information or burning wood from the fire that you may warm yourselves.’”
k_s4a: A fire? And what did Musa find there?
s4a_2: And when he came to it, he was called: “O Musa! Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.” “Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me.”
s4c: Yes, my dear. “And Allah spoke to Musa with direct speech.” That is why he is called Kalimullah: the one to whom Allah spoke. And Allah gave him two signs: his staff became a snake whenever he threw it, and his hand came out white, without any harm, whenever he drew it out from under his arm.
s4d: Then Allah said: “Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.” And Musa prayed: “My Lord, expand for me my breast, and ease for me my task, and untie the knot from my tongue, that they may understand my speech. And appoint for me a minister from my family, Harun, my brother.” And Allah said: “You have been granted your request, O Musa.”
s5a: And Allah said to Musa and Harun: “And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear Allah.” But Pharaoh was arrogant and did not believe, and he gathered the most skilled magicians of his kingdom.
s5b: “And suddenly their ropes and staffs seemed to him from their magic that they were moving.” Then Musa threw his staff, “and at once it devoured what they falsified!”
s5c: Ha! No magic works against Allah’s sign!
s5d: Exactly! “So the magicians fell down in prostration. They said, ‘We have believed in the Lord of Harun and Musa.’” Pharaoh threatened them, but they stood firm.
s6a: Then Allah commanded Musa: “Travel by night with My servants.” Pharaoh caught up with them with his soldiers: “So they pursued them at sunrise.” The sea in front of them, and Pharaoh behind them! “The companions of Musa said, ‘Indeed, we are to be overtaken!’”
s6b: Oh no! And what did Musa do?
s6c: Musa said: “No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me.” “Then We inspired to Musa, ‘Strike with your staff the sea,’ and it parted, and each portion was like a great towering mountain.” And between them was a dry path: “a dry path through the sea”.
s6d: Musa and the Children of Israel crossed safely. And when Pharaoh followed them with his soldiers, the sea closed over them. “And We saved Musa and those with him, all together.”
s6e: The sea split open! This is a great miracle!
s6f: And do you know what? Our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, fasted on the day of Ashura, because on that day Allah saved Musa. And he said, “I am closer to Musa than you,” and he ordered that it be fasted.
s7a: They’ve fallen asleep… When you are afraid, say like Musa: “With me is my Lord.” And when something is hard, pray: “My Lord, expand for me my breast, and ease for me my task.” And always speak gently, even with difficult people.
s7b: And next time, I’ll tell you about Harun, Musa’s eloquent brother… And you, watching us right now: if you liked the story, ask your parents to subscribe to our channel, so you don’t miss the next story.
close: And you, dear fathers and mothers: subscribe to our channel, and share these stories with the people you love, so that together we pass on the beautiful message of Islam to our children.
final: Good night, my dears. I entrust you to Allah, with whom nothing entrusted is ever lost.
